# Run several games at once

Status: InProgress

Different games can start and run at the same time (issue #129). Core publishes one session per launch; the launch feature keeps a stop, an output buffer and after-launch behavior per session; Home shows the current game's own launch moment.

## Scope

- In: Core context publishes every session, keyed per launch
- In: The launch feature keeps one slot per session: cancel, output, after-launch
- In: Home keeps a launch moment per game and shows the current game's
- In: The game page shows and stops its own game
- Out: Several processes of the same game (phase 2: shared launch lease, per-session marker, options.txt and latest.log conflicts, a second-process control)
- Out: Several launcher processes

## Tasks

- [x] T1 — Core: sessions as a list (Completed)
  Acceptance: Context.sessions holds one entry per game; a launch of game B leaves game A's session; a failed session stays until that game starts again; core tests cover both
- [x] T2 — UI: one launch slot per game (Completed)
  Acceptance: Launch keeps cancel and output per game; events name their game; stopping game A leaves B running; the launcher hides when a game runs and comes back only when the last one ends
- [x] T3 — UI: Home and pages per game (Completed)
  Acceptance: Starting game B while A runs is allowed; Home shows the current game's moment; switching the current game shows that game's moment; a running game can not be started twice
- [ ] T4 — Phase 2: several processes of one game (Proposed)
  Acceptance: Decided separately: lease, marker, options capture and log separation designed first

## Validation

- Core and UI tests for concurrent sessions pass
  Result: Passed: lumilio-core context (incl. two_games_publish_their_own_sessions), lumilio-ui launch + shell (incl. two_games_launch_side_by_side_and_end_on_their_own, home_keeps_each_games_launch_moment_while_another_is_current, the dependency table), lumilio-app live; clippy -D warnings clean.
- Real-window spot check: two games run, each stops on its own
  Result: pending

## Decision D1

Different games first; the same game twice is phase 2

Why: Core already keeps a lease per game. A second process of the same game shares its session marker, options.txt capture and logs/latest.log, which need their own design.

Consequences: Starting a game that is already on its way or running is still refused, with its own message.

## Decision D2

Hide on the first running game, come back on the last ending one

Why: Bringing the launcher to the front when one of two games quits covers the game still played.

Consequences: after-launch is read per session; foreground-on-exit waits for no game to be active.
